<task>
You are given a diagram representing the core component of the codebase: the connected set of responsibilities around which the application's main behavior and state are organized.

Your task is to restructure the core component diagram into a canvas: a single central diagram with a couple of peripheral diagrams connected to it.

Framing

A tree diagram can relate components in two ways:

- Vertical (compositional): depth means "is part of". A child is contained in, held by, or owned by its parent. Reading down a branch, you move from a whole into its parts.
- Horizontal (relational): components that interact without one containing the other, e.g. a call into a shared service, a notification to a listener, or data produced by one component and consumed by another.

The core component diagram was generated as a mostly *flat* collection: its components sit side by side as top-level peers, even when one is actually part of another, and the relations between them appear only as inline references. This hides how the system is put together.

Before:

  Podcast player
  |
  |-- LibraryWorkspace
  |   |-- Holds open shows and one PlayerSession per active device
  |   `-- Notifies listeners when a session's queue changes
  |-- PlayerSession
  |   |-- Wraps a PlaybackController
  |   `-- Exposes queue / position / status stores
  |-- PlaybackController
  |   |-- play / pause / seek / enqueue
  |   |-- Holds PlaybackQueue and PlaybackState
  |   `-- Calls AudioEngine.load / start
  |-- PlaybackQueue: ordered episode references
  |-- AudioEngine: decodes and outputs audio; shared by all sessions
  |-- DownloadManager: fetches episodes; AudioEngine reads cached files
  `-- SyncService: listens for queue changes; writes listening progress

After:

  Podcast player
  |
  |-- LibraryWorkspace
  |   `-- PlayerSession (one per active device)
  |       |-- Exposes queue / position / status stores
  |       |   `-- -> notifies SyncService on queue change
  |       `-- PlaybackController
  |           |-- PlaybackQueue: ordered episode references
  |           |-- PlaybackState: position / status
  |           `-- play(episode)
  |               |-- -> AudioEngine.load(cached file)
  |               `-- -> AudioEngine.start()
  |
  |-- AudioEngine (shared service; used by every PlaybackController)
  |   `-- reads files cached by DownloadManager
  |-- DownloadManager
  |   `-- caches episode files -> consumed by AudioEngine.load
  `-- SyncService
      `-- queue changes + PlaybackState.position -> listening progress

1. Restructure the core component diagram into the central diagram
   - Give it a primarily *vertical*, compositional structure: nest each component under the component it belongs to, so the shape of the tree alone shows what the system is made of and how the parts fit together.
   - Do not discard the horizontal relationships. Some components will not nest cleanly (e.g. a shared service used by many parts, or an external producer that acts on a part from outside). Do not force these under a false parent; instead, express the relation as an annotated line at the point in the vertical structure where the interaction happens, e.g. a call or notification line under the specific operation that triggers it.
   - The vertical structure is the skeleton; horizontal relations are laid over it.

2. Pull out concepts that should become their own diagrams
   - Each peripheral diagram should connect to the node in the central diagram, at the depth, that it elaborates.
   - Where a horizontal relation in the central diagram links two pulled-out concepts, connect those peripheral diagrams to each other as well.
</task>
